B
Which molecule remains part of the ribosome through many translation cycles?
mRNA|rRNA|aminoacyl-tRNA|nascent protein
rRNA is an integral structural and catalytic component. The message and charged tRNAs are transient substrates, and the polypeptide is the product.
B
What is the physical dimension of a Svedberg?
Mass|Length|Time|Force
Sedimentation coefficient is velocity divided by acceleration, giving seconds. One S equals 10⁻¹³ s, not a dalton.
B
Which RNA combination identifies a conventional bacterial 50S subunit?
16S and 5S|18S and 5.8S|23S and 5S|28S and 5.8S
23S and 5S are the bacterial large-subunit rRNAs. 16S is small-subunit RNA; 18S, 5.8S and 28S are eukaryotic cytosolic designations.
B
Which rRNA is in the 40S subunit of a typical animal cell?
18S forms the main RNA framework of the 40S particle. 5S and 28S belong to the 60S subunit; 23S is a bacterial reference designation.
B
Which rRNA of a typical eukaryotic cytosolic ribosome is separately transcribed by RNA polymerase III?
5S is separately transcribed; the other three are processed from a polymerase I precursor. The completed particle requires coordinated assembly.
B
The principal bacterial peptidyl-transferase RNA is:
16S|23S|5S|mRNA
The catalytic region is in 23S rRNA of the large subunit. 16S supports decoding, 5S contributes to architecture, and mRNA supplies sequence information.
B
Which statement about a bacterial 70S particle is correct?
It has 70 proteins by definition|Its subunit masses are 30 and 50 Da|Its coefficient is not the sum of the subunit coefficients|It lacks proteins
S is a hydrodynamic coefficient, not a protein count or mass. Association changes friction as well as mass.
B
Which site initially holds the canonical initiator tRNA in an assembled initiation complex?
A|P|E|Exit tunnel
The initiator occupies P, leaving A for the next aminoacyl-tRNA. The tunnel conducts polypeptide, not tRNA.
B
Which molecule provides the nucleophile in ordinary peptide transfer?
The P-site peptide's amino terminus|The A-site amino acid's amino group|The mRNA phosphate|Free ATP
The incoming amino group attacks the carbonyl of the P-site ester. ATP was used in charging; the mRNA is not a chemical substrate for this bond.
B
Immediately following peptide transfer, in the classical site description, where is the elongated chain?
On A-site tRNA|On E-site tRNA|On the original P-site tRNA|Free in the cytosol
Acyl transfer moves the chain to the incoming tRNA. The former P-site tRNA is deacylated; release requires a later reaction.
B
The exit tunnel belongs principally to which ribosomal region?
Small subunit|Large subunit|mRNA channel|E-site anticodon pocket
The large-subunit tunnel conducts the nascent polypeptide. E is a tRNA exit site and is not this tunnel.
B
A tRNA in A/P hybrid state has which arrangement?
Both ends in A|Anticodon in A, acceptor end in P|Anticodon in P, acceptor end in A|Both ends in E
The first letter refers to the small-subunit position; the second to the large-subunit position. Hybrid states arise from coordinated but nonidentical movements.
B
Which is the standard mammalian mitochondrial ribosome designation?
80S|70S in every species|55S|40S
Mammalian mitoribosomes are conventionally 55S. Mitochondrial particles vary among organisms; 80S is cytosolic, and 40S is a cytosolic small subunit.
B
A typical chloroplast ribosome is best described as:
Bacterial-type 70S|Cytosolic 80S attached to thylakoid|A 60S particle only|A membrane-enclosed ribosome
Plastid translation uses a bacterial-related 70S particle. It is not an ER-associated cytosolic ribosome and has two subunits.
B
What distinguishes a polysome from a monosome?
A polysome has only one large subunit|A polysome is several ribosomes on one mRNA|A monosome cannot translate|A polysome makes a single shared peptide
Each particle translates independently on the shared message. A monosome can be productive; each ribosome has its own nascent chain.
B
Which direction is ordinary mRNA read?
3′ to 5′|5′ to 3′|Both directions simultaneously|Determined by drawing orientation
The ribosome advances 5′ to 3′ through the coding region and synthesizes protein N to C, irrespective of diagram orientation.
B
What best describes bacterial 16S A1492/A1493/G530?
Structural contributors to codon recognition|Three amino acids in the tunnel|Enzymes that charge tRNA|Stop codons
These are rRNA nucleotide positions in the decoding region. They are neither proteins nor codons in the message.
B
Why do cytosolic free and ER-associated ribosomes have the same basic architecture?
The membrane converts 70S to 80S|ER-associated particles are cytosolic ribosomes recruited by targeting|ER RNA contains no codons|The ER synthesizes rRNA instead of protein
Targeting recruits an ordinary cytosolic ribosome to the ER surface. It does not change the ribosome into a bacterial-type particle.
B
What is a direct effect of a conventional tetracycline-sensitive target interaction?
Disruption of incoming tRNA accommodation|DNA replication termination|Hydrolysis of completed proteins|Removal of all rRNA
Tetracycline interferes with incoming aa-tRNA at the small-subunit A-site region. The other effects are not its primary ribosomal mechanism.
B
Which pairing of subunit and function is correct?
Small: peptidyl transfer; large: primary decoding|Small: primary decoding; large: peptidyl transfer|Both independently produce full proteins|Large: aminoacyl-tRNA synthesis
The small-subunit environment monitors message-adaptor recognition, and the large subunit positions substrates for transfer. Synthetases charge tRNA before delivery.
B
Which statement best explains the term ribozyme for a ribosome?
It contains no proteins|It translates only RNA enzymes|Its peptide-transfer catalytic environment is principally rRNA|It synthesizes rRNA from DNA
RNA provides the active-site organization. Proteins remain essential to normal assembly and function; RNA is not the translation product.
B
Which molecular event releases a normal completed protein from peptidyl-tRNA?
Aminoacylation of its N terminus|Hydrolysis of its ester linkage|Cleavage of all peptide bonds|Movement of the tRNA through the tunnel
Release factors promote ester hydrolysis, not degradation of the peptide chain. The tRNA exits separately.
B
Which statement about archaeal ribosomes is valid?
All are 80S|70S implies identical bacterial protein composition|They are generally 70S with important molecular similarities to eukaryotic translation systems|They have no rRNA
Sedimentation class is not a complete evolutionary classification. Archaea possess conserved RNA cores and distinct proteins/factors.
B
Which is the strongest direct structural evidence for RNA-centered catalysis?
Ribosomes stain with an RNA dye|Substrate analogs occupy an active site formed by conserved rRNA|Cells have many ribosomes|Translation requires ATP
The substrate-contact geometry directly localizes the catalytic environment. The other observations are compatible with several mechanisms.
B
Why is an rRNA mutation that causes low protein synthesis not automatically proof of direct catalytic participation?
RNA can never catalyze|Assembly or substrate binding may be defective|Mutations cannot change RNA folding|All ribosome activity is independent of structure
A whole-system output is sensitive to many steps. Assembly, binding and catalytic tests must be distinguished.
AR
Assertion: 30S and 50S associate to form 70S. Reason: Sedimentation depends on buoyant mass and friction, and friction changes on association.
Both true; reason explains assertion|Both true; reason does not explain assertion|Assertion true; reason false|Assertion false; reason true
Association changes hydrodynamic properties, so the coefficient is not additive.
AR
Assertion: The P site always contains peptidyl-tRNA. Reason: Peptide transfer leaves the former P-site tRNA deacylated.
Both true; reason explains assertion|Both true; reason does not explain assertion|Assertion true; reason false|Assertion false; reason true
The site name describes a characteristic state, not an invariant occupancy.
AR
Assertion: A heavy polysome profile always indicates high completed-protein output. Reason: Slowed elongation can increase ribosome residence time.
Both true; reason explains assertion|Both true; reason does not explain assertion|Assertion true; reason false|Assertion false; reason true
Occupancy can increase despite low productive flux. The reason exposes the false assertion.
AR
Assertion: Ribosomal proteins can be essential even though the catalytic center is RNA-based. Reason: Proteins stabilize assembly and support the required geometry.
Both true; reason explains assertion|Both true; reason does not explain assertion|Assertion true; reason false|Assertion false; reason true
Catalytic identity and full system sufficiency are distinct.
AR
Assertion: All mitochondrial ribosomes sediment at 55S. Reason: Mammalian mitoribosomes are conventionally 55S.
Both true; reason explains assertion|Both true; reason does not explain assertion|Assertion true; reason false|Assertion false; reason true
The mammalian example is correct, but mitochondrial ribosomes vary among lineages.
MS
Which statements are correct? I: A site spans both subunits. II: The ribosome generally verifies the attached amino acid directly against the codon. III: The initiator starts in P.
I only|I and III|II and III|All three
I and III are true. Aminoacyl identity is largely established upstream by synthetases; the ribosome primarily checks the pairing geometry.
MS
Which statements are correct? I: 5S is in the bacterial large subunit. II: 18S is in the animal 40S. III: 23S is in the animal 40S.
I and II|I and III|II and III|All three
The third is wrong: 23S is the bacterial large-subunit RNA, not animal 40S RNA.
MS
Which statements are correct? I: Polysomes share one mRNA. II: All particles necessarily move at identical speed. III: Each ribosome has its own nascent chain.
I only|II only|I and III|All three
Polysomes have individual chains and shared template; ribosomes can pause or differ in local progression.
M
Match I: 16S; II: 23S; III: 18S; IV: 12S mitochondrial rRNA. a: animal 40S; b: bacterial 30S; c: mammalian mtSSU; d: bacterial 50S.
I-b II-d III-a IV-c|I-d II-b III-c IV-a|I-a II-c III-b IV-d|I-c II-a III-d IV-b
16S is bacterial small-subunit RNA; 23S is bacterial large; 18S is eukaryotic cytosolic small; 12S is mammalian mitochondrial small.
M
Match I: A site; II: P site; III: E site; IV: tunnel. a: nascent-chain route; b: incoming elongator; c: deacylated tRNA departure; d: initial chain-bearing tRNA.
I-b II-d III-c IV-a|I-d II-b III-a IV-c|I-a II-c III-b IV-d|I-c II-a III-d IV-b
These are characteristic site roles. Immediately after transfer A holds peptide and P is deacylated; site names are not absolute.
C
A mutant has normal assembled 70S abundance and tRNA binding but only 8% of wild-type model peptidyl-transfer activity. Which inference is strongest?
Defective DNA replication|A defect at or coupled to the chemical center|No ribosomes were made|All tRNAs were mischarged

The controls reduce the likelihood of assembly or binding defects. The activity assay points toward chemical positioning or catalysis; it does not prove a specific mutated atom acts as an acid or base.
C

A preparation contains equal numbers of intact particles before and after drug treatment. Cognate tRNA accommodation falls to 10%, but an isolated large-subunit model reaction is normal. Which region is implicated first?
Small-subunit-associated delivery/decoding environment|Large-subunit catalytic chemistry exclusively|DNA promoter|Protein degradation
The selective loss of accommodation with preserved model chemistry implicates selection/delivery. A soluble delivery factor could also be involved and must be controlled.
C
A deliberately mischarged Ala-tRNA with its normal anticodon carries glycine and pairs correctly with an alanine codon. What is the expected decoding outcome if accommodated?
Alanine must be incorporated|Glycine can be incorporated|The anticodon automatically changes|The message is edited into a glycine codon
The chemical cargo is glycine; correct pairing does not restore the standard amino-acid assignment. Acceptance efficiency may differ from the natural substrate.
C
Low Mg²⁺ shifts 70S to 30S and 50S; restoring Mg²⁺ restores the peak but not translation. What conclusion follows?
Peak recovery proves activity|Subunit association recovered but functional competence is not established|The small RNA must have been synthesized again|S values measured mass loss
Hydrodynamic association and activity are different endpoints. Check RNA integrity, factor availability and site function.
C
A compensatory double rRNA mutation restores predicted pairing and rescues translation whereas either single mutation lowers activity. Which model is supported?
A structural pairing interaction is important|Both residues must independently donate protons|The gene is not expressed|The RNA is a protein
Rescue by restored complementarity supports a structural requirement. It does not by itself exclude other effects or establish detailed chemistry.
C
A drug blocks new initiation but existing ribosomes elongate normally. What happens to preloaded polysomes over time?
Progressive runoff|All nascent chains instantly vanish|Occupancy necessarily rises|The ribosome becomes 60S only
Completion removes ribosomes without replenishment; heavy polysomes tend to decline. Clearance time depends on message length and elongation.
C
A treatment increases heavy polysomes but lowers complete-protein production. Which explanation fits both?
Increased elongation speed alone|Slower elongation with ribosome accumulation|Loss of all RNA|Increased protein output by definition
Residence time can increase while completion falls, especially with bottlenecks. A time-course or positional assay can test stalling.
C
RNase treatment eliminates heavy polysome peaks but leaves intact monosomes under controlled conditions. Which result is supported?
Heavier particles depended on RNA connecting ribosomes|Peptide bonds were hydrolyzed|All large subunits lacked rRNA|The S values were additive
Preserving intact monosomes while losing heavier complexes supports a shared RNA scaffold. Confirm enzyme specificity and RNA integrity.
C
Two reporters have identical peptide sequence but different synonymous codons near a pause. The pause changes. What is justified?
A message/decoding contribution is plausible|The peptide sequence must have changed|A direct catalytic mutation is proven|The promoter was necessarily altered
Synonymous changes can affect RNA structure, decoding or timing. They may also influence cotranslational folding, so the experiment is not uniquely diagnostic.
C

A cell makes normal cytosolic proteins but mitochondrial-encoded oxidative phosphorylation products fall sharply. Which follow-up most directly distinguishes mitochondrial translation from transcript loss?
Measure mitochondrial RNA abundance and synthesis of new organelle-encoded polypeptides|Count cytosolic ribosomes only|Measure nuclear DNA length|Measure extracellular pH alone
Separating message abundance from new protein output tests whether expression fails at translation rather than transcript supply.
C
A 60S maturation mutant accumulates precursor particles in the nucleus. Cytosolic particles that mature retain normal catalytic activity. What is best supported?
Biogenesis/export defect rather than a direct catalytic defect|All 60S catalytic RNA is absent|Small subunits charge tRNA|Ribosomes are permanently assembled
Localization, abundance and per-particle activity together support a supply or maturation problem.
C
A normal P-site peptidyl-tRNA and a cognate A-site aa-tRNA are present; after one successful transfer but before classical translocation which linkage remains?
Peptide attached to original P tRNA|Elongated peptide attached to A tRNA|Both tRNAs attached covalently to same peptide|No ester link remains
The chain moves to the A-site tRNA, which retains its ester linkage; the former P tRNA becomes uncharged.
C
A mutant small subunit increases near-cognate substitutions using a verified identical aa-tRNA pool. Which alternative remains reasonable?
Defective interaction with a delivery factor|Different supplied amino acid identity as the only explanation|No mRNA exists|Peptide formation cannot occur at all
The controlled pool rules out a difference in pre-existing charging. A ribosome–factor interaction can alter selection, so direct rRNA causation needs more evidence.
N
At ω = 5,000 rad/s and r = 0.08 m, what local velocity corresponds to 70S?
s = 7×10⁻¹² s; acceleration = 25×10⁶×0.08 = 2×10⁶ m/s². u = 1.4×10⁻⁵ m/s = 14 µm/s.
N
Two particles have equal buoyant mass. Particle X has twice the friction of Y. If Y is 60S, X is:
At equal effective mass s is inversely proportional to f. Dividing 60S by two gives 30S.
N
For a single species at unchanged temperature and solvent correction, s increases by 20% and D decreases by 20%. How does the inferred M change?
No change|1.2-fold|1.5-fold|0.8-fold
M ∝ s/D; ratio = 1.2/0.8 = 1.5. Assumes a well-defined species and unchanged other factors.
N
A 300-residue ORF elongates at 10 residues/s with successful initiation every 5 s. Approximate mean occupancy is:
Transit time ≈300/10 = 30 s. J = 0.2/s; N = JT = 6, neglecting queues and terminal dwell.
N
The same 300-residue ORF slows to 5 residues/s; initiation is unchanged and no crowding occurs. Mean occupancy becomes:
T = 60 s; 0.2×60 = 12. In this ideal steady model completion flux remains J, not twice J.
N
An ORF is 900 coding nucleotides. Assume a simple packing model of 30 nt per particle, no end corrections. The maximum approximate capacity is:
900/30 = 30. This is a simplified geometric bound, not an expected cellular occupancy.
N
A message carries an average of 8 translating ribosomes with residence time 40 s, no premature release. What is the steady completion flux per message?
J = N/T = 8/40 = 0.2 per second, or 12 per minute. Occupancy is not product flux.
N
With fixed angular speed and coefficient, a particle moves at 6 µm/s at radius 0.05 m. At 0.10 m its local speed is:
3 µm/s|6 µm/s|12 µm/s|24 µm/s
u = sω²r, so doubling r doubles local velocity when s and ω remain constant.
